report.speaker: Tom Hutchcroft
report.title: Dimension Dependence of Critical Phenomena in Long-Range Percolation
report.question: 长程渗流的两点连接、临界簇体积和尺度极限怎样随空间维数与长边衰减指数变化？
report.reading_scope: Published SIAM PDF, volume 5 pp.462–482: entire actual text of §§1–4, all displayed formulas and captions, acknowledgments and bibliography [1]–[104], read from complete raw extraction in overlapping sections; mathematical body cross-checked against the entire arXiv:2510.03951v1 PDF text. Publisher pp.474–476 visually inspected to verify the scale table and Theorems 4.3–4.10. No full-page visual audit or complete SIAM HTML reading claimed. Supplemental I: actual PDF §I.1.3 pp.9–12, including (HD), Theorem I.1.6, canonical measure and I.1.9; for HUT-R2 also Definition I.1.3/I.1.5 excerpts pp.6–8 and Lemma I.4.1 with its proof and (I.4.4), pp.33–34, plus limited pp.41–42 excerpts. No full proof-section reading claimed. Supplemental II: actual PDF introduction pp.9–14 through Theorem II.1.13 and the start of II.1.14 only. Supplemental III: abstract and metadata only.

4E01.scope: Countable product construction and countable-union measurability of finite-path connection; no infinite-volume phase theorem.

4E02.scope: Uniform coupling, monotonicity and positivity-set threshold; no claim about continuity at the critical parameter.

4E03.scope: Dyadic kernel sum and finite expected degree imply almost-sure local finiteness.

4E04.scope: Indicator expansion and monotone convergence, allowing infinite values.

4E05.scope: Tail-sum identities, discrete increments and power/logarithm convergence boundary.

4E06.scope: Logarithmic exponent convention, eta, delta including infinity, and moment-ratio definition of d_f.

4E07.scope: Offspring law, independent increments, spatial occupancy and distinction from a percolation cluster.

4E08.scope: Conditional one-generation recursion and monotone summation; no invariance principle.

4E09.scope: Extinction fixed-point limit, Catalan reflection counting and product bounds yielding n^(-1/2) tail comparability.

4E0A.scope: Lattice-shell cardinality comparison and convergent geometric sums for the stated ball and tail power laws with 0<a<d.

4E0B.scope: Convolution upper bound and disjoint-box divergence for the exact deterministic power kernel; not the external theorem that a triangle condition implies mean-field exponents.

4E0C.scope: Conjectural crossover and effective-dimension regime picture, with one-dimensional exceptions distinguished.

4E0D.scope: Complete algebra from explicitly assumed hyperscaling and eta=2-alpha; validity of hyperscaling is not proved here.

4E0E.scope: Definitions of chi, zeta and small-order radii; direct-edge lower bound proves divergence of spatial moments q>=alpha. Sharpness is an external input.

4E0F.scope: Exact three alternatives of (HD+), with logarithm regularized only at bounded distances.

4E10.scope: Theorem 4.1 cited; local power comparison implies eta>=2-alpha when eta exists. The runaway-cluster mechanism is a proof outline only.

4E11.scope: Theorem 4.2 with distinct-point restriction; delta/eta interpretation and block-to-point mechanism are not a reconstruction of the research proof.

4E12.scope: Independent-edge product and exact exponential no-connection law for 0<=beta<infinity. The scale-uniform positive merger bound assumes fixed 0<beta<infinity independent of r, with comparison constants allowed to depend on beta. Conditioning on cross-edge-dependent random clusters is excluded.

4E13.scope: Exact integral and monotone coupling proved; strict subcriticality of finite cutoffs at finite beta_c and finiteness of all cluster moments are cited inputs.

4E14.scope: Finite product differentiation and closed-edge hazard conversion; direct p parameter requires (1-p)^(-1).

4E15.scope: Complete finite translation-invariant torus proof by sum of squared cluster masses; infinite-volume differentiation and limit exchange remain research inputs.

4E16.scope: Complete reciprocal integration for positive C1 functions under the stated asymptotic derivative and divergence hypotheses. Its cutoff-moment application uses the piecewise integration/local absolute-continuity justification in 4E19, not a global C1 assertion about cutoff moments.

4E17.scope: Complete fixed-dilation integration for positive C1 functions on a tail interval; logarithmic-factor counterexamples. Its cutoff-moment application uses the piecewise integration/local absolute-continuity justification in 4E19, not a global C1 assertion about cutoff moments.

4E18.scope: Complete exact ODE integration for a positive C1 function with an integrable remainder; the true percolation coefficient 1/2 is not derived here.

4E19.scope: Moment ODE and moment-ratio asymptotics are cited; the ordinary derivative asymptotic is used only outside D={||z||:z in Z^d minus 0}, hence almost everywhere. Cited strict-subcritical finite moments and the infinite-volume derivative identity I.4.1 imply continuity, a locally bounded piecewise-continuous derivative and local absolute continuity; the domination bound and integration across the locally finite breakpoints are supplied locally. The abstract C1 arguments of 4E16/4E17 then apply piece by piece, without global C1 regularity for the cutoff moments. The p=2 coefficient arithmetic is local; asymptotic independence, higher-moment recursion and second-order errors remain research inputs. All four high/critical/marginal regimes are unchanged.

4E1A.scope: Theorem 4.3 cited with all HD+ hypotheses; delta=2, almost-sure finite cluster and divergent mean follow locally from the tail.

4E1B.scope: Complete integrating-factor solution of an exact C1 ODE and three asymptotic cases; actual spatial-moment error estimates not supplied.

4E1C.scope: Definition for a finite cutoff with finite susceptibility and normalization of the weighted vertex law.

4E1D.scope: Finite beta_c and every positive-order cutoff radius bounded by its cutoff length; not an identification with the conjectural full Sak region.

4E1E.scope: Theorem 4.6 with the conditional if-and-only-if region and alpha>d exclusion; no assertion at alpha=d beyond the stated conditions.

4E1F.scope: Theorem 4.7 cited; shell bound on the numerator proved, while the susceptibility lower bound needed for the reverse implication remains explicit external input.

4E20.scope: Theorem 4.8 cited, including the conditional alpha=d discontinuous boundary clarified by II. Local extraction of delta and d_f; large-cluster lower bounds and hyperscaling proof are external.

4E21.scope: Complete logarithmic exponent contradiction from three stated deterministic moment bounds; no derivation of the bounds.

4E22.scope: Theorem 4.9 cited; equilateral-distance exponents substituted locally. Gladkov inequality is a separately cited input from the research paper.

4E23.scope: Theorem 4.10 cited with the existence premise and small-q convention; summation provides motivation, not the full off-critical comparison proof.

4E24.scope: Finite mass measure, all bounded-continuous test functions, and the second-level weak topology for laws; no tightness theorem.

4E25.scope: Canonical measure described via a fixed-normalization binary branching-random-walk scaling construction; existence and convergence are quoted, not proved. Mass cutoff and time-integrated meaning explained.

4E26.scope: Theorem 4.4 in all four HD+-restricted normalization regimes. Local probability conditioning uses finite nonzero limiting mass; genealogy/internal distances not asserted.

4E27.scope: Complete parameter checks and arithmetic consequences of quoted theorems, contrasted with alpha=2/3 critical-dimensional tail.

4E28.scope: Nearest-neighbor logarithmic exponents and epsilon expansions retained as predictions as presented in this report edition; no claim of a proof or later-status survey.

4E29.scope: Dyadic computation of jump second moment and truncated logarithmic divergence at alpha=2; not a proof of Sak crossover.

Locally supplied arguments cover finite-volume calculus, conditional ODE integrations, and cutoff continuity/local absolute continuity from the cited derivative identity and finite moments.

Full CL characterization proofs, cutoff lower bounds, low-dimensional hyperscaling and cluster-volume lower bounds, k-point/Gladkov estimates, off-critical relations. Precise introduction statements on pp.9–14 were read; §§II.2–II.6 proofs were not read in full or reproduced.

metadata.model_conventions: Euclidean Z^d, J(x,y)=||x-y||^(-d-alpha), independent probabilities 1-exp(-beta J), full-kernel beta_c, continuous length cutoff J_r. Positive C1 hypotheses belong to the abstract elementary integration lemmas; actual cutoff moments use ordinary derivatives away from lattice-distance radii and are locally absolutely continuous, as justified in 4E19. The constant-order merger consequence fixes positive beta independently of r. HD+, CL, distinct vertices and finite-beta_c cutoff assumptions are explicit. Marginal d=6 alpha=2 separated from LR CD d=3alpha<6; alpha=d retained only as a conditional CL boundary.

source_records.actual_reading: Locally written proofs in the explicitly identified atoms; no imported full research proof.
source_records.proof_boundary: Finite/countable product calculations, dyadic power sums in their stated ranges, a binary branching example, finite-graph differentiation, conditional C1 ODE calculus, and local continuity/piecewise integration consequences of the cited infinite-volume cutoff derivative identity. No a=0 logarithmic-borderline proof is claimed for 4E0A.

source_clarifications.resolution: Published report is volume 5 pp.462–482, CC BY 4.0. The corresponding arXiv v1 and three supplemental preprints retain their separate arXiv licenses. No original figures are copied. Chinese adaptation and independently written elementary arguments are attributed in the reference node.

I uses a kernel/norm normalization different from the report. 4E19 keeps the report coefficient v_d(d+alpha)beta_c. I.1.6 supplies the regime and absence of a second-moment logarithm in the conditional doubly marginal case; I.4.1 supplies the derivative identity in terms of the actual kernel derivative. Normalized constants are not copied between conventions.

source_clarifications.location: II v1 PDF versus generated HTML
source_clarifications.resolution: The observed HTML rendering carried a date different from the fixed v1 PDF; claims are pinned to the downloaded v1 PDF and its digest, not that generated date.
Conditional calculations 4E0D, 4E16–4E18, 4E1B and 4E21 prove only their explicit assumptions. Theorems 4.1–4.10 are accurately usable research inputs, not labeled as locally fully proved.

Ordinary derivatives are used only outside the locally finite lattice-distance set D, hence almost everywhere. Strict-subcritical cutoff moment bounds and cited I.4.1 yield continuous, piecewise C1, locally absolutely continuous moments. The C1 calculus proofs in 4E16/4E17 extend by finite-piece integration and cancellation at continuous endpoints. No global C1 regularity or change in the moment exponents is asserted.

source_errata.issue: In direct Bernoulli p parametrization, the displayed closed-edge increment lacks the factor (1-p)^(-1).
source_errata.resolution: 4E14 proves the corrected finite-product formula; 4E15 proves the susceptibility identity. In exponential beta-J parametrization the closed-edge factor cancels against p prime, so the report cutoff derivative keeps its stated coefficient.

source_errata.issue: The displayed singular power cannot be applied at x=y despite the unrestricted all-pairs wording.
source_errata.resolution: 4E11 restricts to distinct vertices, as required by the two-point power law.
4E0F and 4E19 use log(2+||x-y||), equivalent at large distances with bounded-distance constants absorbed.

source_errata.issue: A hierarchical critical two-point exponent is printed with -d-alpha, inconsistent with the long-range critical exponent discussed there.
source_errata.resolution: No hierarchical theorem is imported into this packet. The Euclidean results use the explicit Theorems 4.2 and 4.7 with -d+alpha; this possible source typo is recorded rather than silently used.

source_errata.issue: The printed higher-moment sign is inconsistent with positive gamma and the positive moment-gap exponent convention.
source_errata.resolution: 4E0E defines Delta directly through zeta=E|K|^2/E|K| following II §II.1.3; the inconsistent higher-moment display is not reproduced.

source_errata.issue: The year 2024 is printed for arXiv:2508.18807.
source_errata.resolution: Reference and source record use the actual v1 submission date 2025-08-26.

section_coverage.scope: Motivation from branching and independent-walk dimension dependence; SAW/Ising retained only as background.
Percolation, critical exponents, branching comparison, triangle power counting, hyperscaling algebra, probability differentiation and conjectural short-range critical logs.
Power-law model, local finiteness, jump-variance threshold, effective dimension and Sak crossover prediction.
Average and pointwise two-point results plus accessible direct merging probability.

Cutoff construction, finite differentiation, ordinary moment derivatives away from locally finite activation radii, justified piecewise/local-AC integration, conditional ODE calculations, and cited moment/tail results with exact regimes.
Spatial-moment resonance, measure topology, canonical excursion measure, four normalization regimes and conditional weak convergence.
Cutoff gyration, CL definition and known domain, full/cutoff two-point theorem and shell numerator estimate.
Low-dimensional cluster mass, exponent contradiction, three-point regimes, precise subcritical exponent definitions/relations, explicit two-dimensional example.

remaining_branches.scope: Report §1 uses these for universality motivation; separate model definitions and research proofs are not developed in this percolation packet.
§4 historical hierarchical results and general slowly varying/anisotropic kernels are not expanded; the notes use the exact Euclidean power kernel of the report.

The report statement for three-point functions and leading exponent relations is covered; the research series general k-point, quantitative off-critical and correction estimates are not fully developed.

remaining_branches.branch: Sak crossover and low-dimensional scaling limits
remaining_branches.scope: Full characterization of CL, short-range universality after crossover, uniqueness/conformal structure of low-dimensional scaling limits, and nearest-neighbor six-dimensional log predictions remain open/conjectural in the pinned report.

unexpanded_deep_proofs.scope: Sharp subcritical finite cluster moments and strict subcriticality of the finite-range cutoff at finite beta_c.
Universal tightness/large-cluster control and the space-average-to-pointwise two-point estimates.

Infinite-volume derivative exchange is retained as the I.4.1/sharpness research input; asymptotic independence, all-moment recursion, second-order critical errors, Tauberian transfer, mixed spatial moments, tightness and superprocess identification remain unexpanded. Locally supplied arguments cover finite-volume calculus, conditional ODE integrations, and cutoff continuity/local absolute continuity from the cited derivative identity and finite moments.

Full CL characterization proofs, cutoff lower bounds, low-dimensional hyperscaling and cluster-volume lower bounds, k-point/Gladkov estimates, off-critical relations. Precise introduction statements on pp.9–14 were read; §§II.2–II.6 proofs were not read in full or reproduced.

Construction/uniqueness and branching-random-walk convergence to canonical integrated superprocess excursion measures. Canonical-measure introduction pp.11–12 and the report background were read, not the full superprocess proof literature.
